findings.title: Backup codes unusable for Google/SAML users with 2FA
findings.body: In the credentials authorize flow, the identity-provider guards run before the backup-code branch and only check `credentials.totpCode`: `user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode` throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled, and `!user.password && ... && !credentials.totpCode` throws IncorrectEmailPassword. A Google/SAML user with 2FA enabled who loses their authenticator and submits a backup code (the `/auth/login?totp=...` flow sends no totpCode) will be rejected before the backup-code check at line 131 is ever reached, and such users also have no password to fall back on. The guards should also pass when `credentials.backupCode` is present.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic
findings.body: The login flow decrypts the code list, checks `indexOf`, and then updates the user row in a separate, non-transactional step. Two concurrent login requests presenting the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either writes back, allowing a single-use code to be used twice. The copy in the UI explicitly promises each code "can be used exactly once". Consider an atomic update or a conditional update keyed on the stored value.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message instructs an impossible action
findings.body: The new string "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." tells users to generate backup codes in settings, but this PR adds no way to (re)generate backup codes from settings — codes are only created during initial 2FA setup. A user who hits this error (e.g. 2FA enabled before this feature existed, so `backupCodes` is null) is directed to an action that does not exist.

findings.title: No test coverage for logging in with a backup code
findings.body: The PR's core security feature — consuming a backup code during login and enforcing single-use — has no test. The added tests only cover the download/copy buttons on the setup screen, and the file itself acknowledges this with a TODO. A regression in the authorize backup-code branch (e.g. the identity-provider guard issue) would not be caught.
